styles.city: A page from an explorer's field sketchbook, drawn on the spot, in the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries (Cook's artists, Conrad Martens on the Beagle, Thomas Baines with Livingstone, Edward Wilson in the Antarctic). A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink over parts of it, with loose parallel hatching for shade; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green and faded blue, pooling and leaving the paper bare in places. The drawing is unfinished: detail is concentrated on the city, and the edges, the sky and the near water dissolve into bare cream paper in an irregular vignette. Slightly foxed, worn sketchbook paper with soft tone variation; a single page, no binding or spine visible. An observed working sketch, not a finished painting. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, dates or signature. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given.
styles.journey: An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found. The traveller need not appear: some pages record only what the party saw (a harbour, a fortress, a market, an animal or plant). When the traveller does appear, draw them in action and in a natural, varied pose, not standing to attention. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.
styles.invention: One landscape 3:2 page from an explorers field sketchbook. Visible loose graphite construction lines, quick sepia ink and parallel hatching, restrained uneven watercolour washes in ochre, grey-green and faded blue. Detail concentrated on the principal object or action; outer edges dissolve irregularly into warm cream paper with subtle foxing. An observed working sketch, not a polished painting, digital render, photograph, infographic or collage. A single coherent principal scene, optionally one small unlabelled detail study. No frame, binding, captions, labels, signature, watermark or readable writing. Any marks on historic artifacts remain small and nonverbal. People, materials and tools appropriate to the place and date.
styles.natural: Create ONE landscape 3:2 natural-history field sketchbook page. The real named landscape is the subject; preserve its characteristic landforms and plausible scale. Vary foreground and depth according to the scene. Use loose visible graphite construction lines, fine quick sepia ink and parallel hatching, restrained uneven watercolour washes of ochre, grey-green and faded blue, with colour concentrated on the landform. Irregular unfinished vignette edges dissolve into bare subtly worn warm cream paper. A working observational landscape sketch, not a photograph, digital render, fantasy illustration or glossy travel poster. No border, binding, captions, labels, dates, signature, watermark or readable writing. No modern tourist infrastructure, generic explorer portrait or invented landmarks. Do not merge several incompatible viewpoints into one scene.
styles.built: ONE landscape 3:2 architectural field-sketchbook page. Clearly visible loose graphite construction lines, quick sepia ink and parallel hatching, restrained uneven watercolor washes of ochre, grey-green and faded blue. Detail concentrated on the named structure; irregular unfinished edges fade into bare warm cream paper. An observed hand-drawn working sketch, NOT a photograph, glossy painting, digital render, fantasy concept art or infographic. One coherent perspective, believable load-bearing geometry and consistent scale. No border, binding, labels, captions, date, signature, watermark or readable text. Only tiny indistinct marks for inscriptions. No modern tourism infrastructure unless explicitly part of scene. People optional, small and appropriate to depicted date, never obligatory foreground explorer.
